response: The international normalised ratio (INR) is not entirely reliable. According to the available data, technical problems associated with INR testing within primary care were not found, but discrepant INR results can be problematic in both hospital and primary care settings. The main issue lies in the lack of standardization when different techniques and reagents are used, which can lead to inconsistent results. To improve the reliability of INR testing, close links between hospital laboratories and primary care practices are necessary, particularly in terms of training and quality assurance. Therefore, while INR can be a useful tool, its reliability depends on the consistency of the methods and reagents used.
